headline: Approved a bid waiver to hire National Golf Foundation as transitional golf course management consultant, and agreed to issue $68 million in bonds.
summary: The golf course closing is set for November 2, and the city needs a consultant to help decide its management model. The mayor received quotes from three firms and said National Golf Foundation best fits the scope and is reasonably priced. The city's municipal advisor recommended a 4.5% rate for projections, up from the 3.75% estimate used in the 2027 CIP process.
decisions: Approved a bid waiver to National Golf Foundation for a transitional management consultant by voice vote with no opposition.
Agreed by consensus to issue $68 million in bonds.

City of Bristol 
Special Board of Finance Meeting Minutes 
October 1, 2026 
 
A special meeting of the Board of Finance was held on Tuesday, October 1, 2026 at 5 p.m. in the 3rd 
Floor Meeting Room of City Hall and via Zoom.  The following were in attendance: Chairman Dave 
Maikowski, Mayor Ellen Zoppo Sassu, Commissioners Marie O’Brien, Jane Murdock, and Bill 
Campion. Commissioners Jon Mace, Mike Massarelli, Mark Peterson and Dante Tagareillo were on 
Zoom. Also present from the Comptroller’s Office: Diane Waldron. 
 
 
       Agenda 
1. Call to order 
2. City Council: 
a. Approval of a bid waiver to National Golf Foundation and to take any action as 
necessary. 
3. Update on Bond Issue and Current Market Issues and to take any action as necessary. 
4. Adjournment 
 
 
1. Call to order 
 
Chairman Maikowski called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m. 
 
 
2. City Council: 
a. Approval of a bid waiver to National Golf Foundation and to take any action as 
necessary. 
 
 
Mayor Zoppo Sassu stated the closing is scheduled for November 2nd and there is a significant 
amount of work to do before then to decide on the management model for the golf course. In order to 
facilitate short term issues and set up for long term success of the management model the city is 
looking to hire a transitional management consultant. National Golf Foundation is a well-respected 
consultant for policy and analysis. The Mayor did receive quotes from three firms and this one has 
dthe best match for the scope and is reasonably priced. 
 
Commissioner O’Brien made a motion seconded by Commissioner Campion 
 
“To approve a bid waiver to National Golf Foundation for a transitional management consultant.”  
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried
October 1, 2026 
Board of Finance Minutes 
 
 
 
3. Update on Bond Issue and Current Market Issues and to take any action as necessary. 
 
 
Diane provided an updated on the debt issue she is preparing as there has been significant volatility in 
the bond market last week.  Another community did a competitive bond issue similar in size to 
Bristol’s and issued at around 4.2%.   The City’s Municipal Advisor is recommending a rate of 4.5% 
for projection purposes. This compares to 3.75% which was the original estimate used during the 
2027 CIP process and will increase Debt Service for 2028 above the gradual planned increase. 
Commissioner Peterson questioned where the increase to non-golf course debt service comes from, 
which is general fud tax dollars. The consensus of the Board was to go ahead and issue the bonds at 
$68 million. 
 
4. Adjournment 
 
 
Commissioner O’Brien made a motion seconded by Commissioner Campion 
 
“To adjourn at 5:40 p.m.” 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.  
 
Attest: 
 
 
Diane M. Waldron 
Board of Finance Clerk
